title: Why Did the British Exile a Tamil Rebel's Son? | Maruthu Brothers, 1801 #shorts

lines.text: Why did the British exile a Tamil rebel's son?
Sivaganga, eighteen oh one. The Maruthu brothers, Periya and Chinna Maruthu, rose against the East India Company.
That June, a proclamation was pasted on the walls of Srirangam temple and Trichy fort, calling people to rise.
lines.caps: that *June | a *proclamation | on the walls | *Srirangam | *Trichy fort | *rise!

lines.text: By autumn, the revolt was crushed.
In late October, the brothers were hanged at Tiruppattur fort. Accounts say sons and followers died with them.
lines.caps: late *October | *hanged | at *Tiruppattur | accounts say | *sons | and *followers | too.

lines.text: About seventy three prisoners, some say seventy two, were put on a ship to Penang, an island off Malaya.
lines.caps: about *73 | *prisoners | some say *72 | on a *ship | to *Penang.

lines.text: Among them, accounts say, was Duraisamy, the young son of Chinna Maruthu, or of his brother.
lines.caps: among them | accounts say | *Duraisamy | a *young *son | of Chinna Maruthu | or his *brother?

lines.text: One study says the exiles were kept alongside convicts there, and fought to keep their rank and dignity.
lines.caps: one *study | kept with | *convicts | fighting for | *rank | and *dignity.

lines.text: What became of most of them is barely recorded.
Mercy, or a punishment worse than the rope? Tell me below. Then watch again, and count who never came home.
